findings.issue: GET /api/tenants/:slug handler does a plain pool.connect() and issues SELECT id, slug FROM choros.tenant WHERE slug = $1 LIMIT 1 WITHOUT setting the choros.tenant_id GUC. choros.tenant has FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (migration 013): policy = id = current_setting('choros.tenant_id', true)::uuid. Without the GUC, current_setting returns NULL, the predicate is always false, every tenant row is invisible to choros_app. Result: POST /api/tenants creates the tenant (withTenantTx sets the GUC correctly), but the immediately following GET /api/tenants/:slug returns 404 for any slug OTHER than those already in the connection's session GUC. The applyPack flow breaks at 'Resolve tenant UUID' step for every test tenant (AC-7/8/9/R-1 in seed-pack.test.ts all fail with 'Cannot resolve tenant: 404'). Confirmed by fitness:db run: 4/5 seed-pack.test.ts tests fail. AC-10 passes because it uses withClient(migratorUrl()) — choros_migrator is table owner and bypasses FORCE RLS. The schema.test and genesis-owner-seed failures in fitness:db are pre-existing (Flowable ACT_ tables present in dev Docker + grant count reflects accumulated dev silo state) and not introduced by T-0140.
findings.suggestion: GET /api/tenants/:slug must set the GUC before the SELECT. Since the slug is known but the UUID is not yet known, the handler cannot use withTenantTx (which needs the UUID). Options: (a) use withTenantTx with a two-step approach — first resolve the tenant id as choros_migrator (via a separate DB role) or (b) query as the pool connection but use SET LOCAL choros.tenant_id = ... for all possible UUIDs (not viable). Practical options: (1) Add a choros_migrator pool (already used in fitness tests) or expose a server-internal query that bypasses RLS for the lookup (analogous to how org-structure tests use withClient(migratorUrl())); (2) have POST /api/tenants return the created tenant's ID in the 201 body (it already does: {id, slug}) and have the importer store the id from the 201 response without a subsequent GET; (3) add a SECURITY DEFINER function that looks up tenant by slug without RLS. Option (2) is already implemented — POST returns {id, slug} — so importer.ts applyPack can simply store tenantId from the 201 body instead of making a separate GET. This is the zero-new-code fix and does not change the public API surface. The GET endpoint would still be useful but needs a RLS-bypass mechanism for correctness.

r1_authz_judgment.question: Is tenant_id from DELETE body an authz hole or correct per ADR?
r1_authz_judgment.reasoning: Auth gate (loadAdminContext → isGenesisOwner) executes BEFORE body is parsed. Any non-genesis-owner caller receives 403 before body.tenant_id is ever read. A genesis-owner caller can delete org entities in any tenant by design: ADR §2.3 option C explicitly places org-structure bootstrap authority on the isGenesisOwner boolean (DB-resolved), not on a per-resource grant. ADR §6 explicitly lists DELETE endpoints as operating under isGenesisOwner gate. The silo model (runtime_target=local/dev-container) means there is no multi-tenant production surface where this pattern would be exploitable. The blast-radius (genesis-owner can name any tenant_id in body) is the intended authority envelope for the seed-reset use case — genesis-owner created those tenants in the first place. No new authority subsystem, no hardcoded slug bypass. FF-6 passes (no e-owner slug comparison). Within ADR §2.3/§6 scope.

role_gap_evidence: Confirmed pattern from R-6: RLS-protected tables are not directly queryable by a plain pool.connect() / choros_app connection without the tenant_id GUC. Any handler that needs to look up a tenant row by slug (a cross-tenant lookup by definition, since the GUC must already equal the tenant's own id for the row to be visible) requires a privileged connection path. Candidate for ledgers/role-gaps.md: 'cross-tenant lookup by slug (pre-UUID-known) requires choros_migrator path or SECURITY DEFINER function — choros_app cannot perform this lookup without a GUC it cannot know without the row.' This is a systemic gap that will recur whenever a new slug-lookup is needed before the UUID is known.
